title: Running OpenClaw in Containers — Kubernetes for Personal AI Agents
speaker: Sally Omali
speaker_role: Principal Software Engineer, Red Hat (Emerging Tech org, AI focus)

key_discoveries.title: Double-Secrets Pattern: Podman Secret + OpenClaw secret_ref
key_discoveries.description: Two-layer secrets architecture where raw API keys live in Podman secrets (or Docker envvars) on the host and OpenClaw's secret_ref config creates a pointer, not a raw value. Keys never appear in OpenClaw logs, config files, git history, or backup archives. Key rotation is 'podman secret rm && podman secret create' with no config edits. Directly adoptable today using macOS Keychain as the host layer even without containers.

key_discoveries.title: Forever Claw: Personal Long-Running Agent Reference Deployment
key_discoveries.description: Omali's home setup — Mclaw (main instance in Montreal), Joy (Jyotish astrology sub-agent for weekly readings), Bruno (Boston Bruins daily NHL playoff briefings) — all containerized with nightly volume backups via launchd. Personal infrastructure story that proves the pattern scales from hobby to enterprise without architectural change.

key_discoveries.title: Volume-Based Backup Story — Podman Volume → Kubernetes PVC
key_discoveries.description: All runtime state (conversation history, memory, skills, MCP state, SSH known_hosts) lives in a single named Podman volume. Backup = snapshot volume. Restore = restore volume. Same mental model carries through from Podman volume on a laptop to PVC on OpenShift with zero architectural change. Directly applicable to our tmux setup today by treating _bmad/ and ~/.claude/projects/<project>/ as 'the volume'.

key_discoveries.title: Enterprise Workspace Base Template Pattern
key_discoveries.description: Platform team curates a baseline OpenClaw image with company-approved MCP servers, authentication, skills, and policy. New hires run podman run (or oc apply) on day one and get the team's standard agent pre-connected to Jira, GitHub, Slack, SSO. Updates propagate through image tags. Replaces the 'sit next to someone and copy their repo' anti-pattern with a curated, versioned, portable onboarding artifact. Maps 1:1 to our future SaaS client Enterprise Workspace roadmap.

key_discoveries.title: SSH-Box Inside the Container (Double Isolation)
key_discoveries.description: Agent runs inside a container (sandbox layer 1) AND routes risky command execution over SSH into a second sandboxed box via a dedicated keypair (sandbox layer 2). Container isolates agent from host; SSH box isolates destructive commands from the container. Adopt even without containers using Lima/OrbStack as the SSH-sandbox target; wire DCG (Destructive Command Guard) to divert matched commands into the box instead of blocking them.

key_discoveries.title: Same Install Tool, Local → Kubernetes → OpenShift
key_discoveries.description: Omali's installer tool targets Podman locally, Docker as fallback, kind for local Kubernetes dev, and OpenShift for enterprise — without configuration divergence between substrates. Named per-instance containers with configurable ports, secrets, and MCP servers. Gives a straight-line path from 'personal agent on my laptop' to 'multi-tenant agent hosting for SaaS clients'.

key_discoveries.title: NVIDIA Case Study: 10 Engineers, 10 Kubernetes OpenClaw Model Eval Instances
key_discoveries.description: NVIDIA runs model evaluation agents as 10 concurrent Kubernetes-hosted OpenClaw instances — periodic checks on model eval status reported back to a small engineering team. Omali's framing: 'doing the job of six engineers with one himself.' First public data point on production multi-instance agent deployment at Kubernetes scale and validates the per-tenant PVC + per-tenant secrets pattern for multi-tenant SaaS scenarios.

key_discoveries.title: Harness/Exec Co-location Fix Is Containers, Not Permissions
key_discoveries.description: Complements Ubl's opening keynote critique ('harness and exec in the same trust boundary = 1999-era security hole'). Omali's answer is operational: the container IS the trust boundary. You can still give the agent --dangerously-skip-permissions *inside* the container because the container itself is sandboxed from the host. Inverts the security debate from 'don't give agents full permission' to 'give them full permission inside an isolated substrate.'

key_discoveries.title: OTel + Jaeger Observability Sidecar as Install-Tool Option
key_discoveries.description: Optional OpenTelemetry collector and Jaeger trace visualizer sidecar wired in by the installer tool. Claude Code's OTel support is mature enough that this is a config change, not a rewrite. Gives full agent trace inspection for free when running 3+ concurrent workers. Immediately useful for our orchestrator's /debug command when the current tmux capture-pane approach hits its limits.

key_discoveries.title: Model Swapping Is Free — Harness Is the Durable Investment
key_discoveries.description: OpenRouter integration makes GPT/Gemma/Claude/local-model swapping a config change. Omali specifically endorses Gemma as 'great' for her day-to-day workloads — notable because the rest of AIE Europe 2026 was Claude- and GPT-centric. Validates Ubl's model-commoditization thesis and suggests cost-sensitive worker lanes (linting, formatting, doc generation) should route to Gemma via OpenRouter while reserving Opus for the work that needs it.

notable_quotes: I'd just rather have it in a container — I don't like putting stuff on my computer.
That's what Red Hat does — if we can't take an application and run it securely, come on, this is our golden opportunity.
People say it's hard to spin up OpenClaw. That took two seconds.
Yes, we're going to AI workloads running everywhere.
Guys, AI is 1000x better than me at writing code.
I don't need to write tedious code anymore — I get to do fun stuff.

adoptable_patterns.name: Podman Secrets + OpenClaw secret_ref Double Layer
adoptable_patterns.description: Host secret store holds raw keys; agent config holds pointers. Log-safe, rotation-cheap, portable. Works today with macOS Keychain as the host layer even without containers.

adoptable_patterns.name: Curated Team Workspace Baseline
adoptable_patterns.description: Platform-engineered baseline image (or template repo as pre-container version) with approved MCP servers, skills, agent personas, and policy. New engineers inherit and personalize.

adoptable_patterns.name: Volume-Based Backup Story (Podman → PVC)
adoptable_patterns.description: All runtime state in one named volume, nightly snapshot via launchd, restore is one command. Pre-container version: treat _bmad/ and ~/.claude/projects/ as the volume, add nightly tar.gz backup job.

adoptable_patterns.name: Kubernetes Deployment Pattern for Enterprise
adoptable_patterns.description: Package orchestrator as image, run on OpenShift/kind, per-tenant PVCs and secrets, namespace isolation. Same install tool, same config surface. NVIDIA model-eval deployment as reference case study.

adoptable_patterns.name: SSH-Box Inside Container (Double Isolation)
adoptable_patterns.description: Second sandbox layer for destructive command execution. Adopt via Lima/OrbStack VM with dedicated SSH keypair; wire DCG to divert matched commands into the box.

adoptable_patterns.name: OTel + Jaeger Observability Sidecar
adoptable_patterns.description: Optional observability stack for agent traces; replaces tmux capture-pane gymnastics when running 3+ concurrent workers. Config change, not a rewrite.

deep_dive_candidates.reason: Podman Secrets reference — foundation for the double-secrets pattern; concrete command surface for host-layer implementation
OpenRouter model routing used in the demo for Gemma/Claude/GPT swapping; worth cataloguing as infrastructure tool
Jaeger trace visualizer for the OTel observability sidecar pattern
PVC reference for the Kubernetes port of the volume-backup pattern
OpenClaw secret_ref feature specifically — need to confirm the exact config surface and whether Claude Code or Pi has equivalent indirection

relevance_context: HIGH if we want enterprise/Kubernetes deployment of our orchestrator (SaaS client multi-tenancy, NVIDIA-style model-eval parallel instances). MEDIUM for current tmux-based architecture on a single Mac. The secrets and volumes patterns are directly applicable regardless of substrate and can be adopted this week via macOS Keychain + launchd nightly backups. The container migration itself is a Phase 3+ decision tied to our enterprise roadmap.
key_insight: Containers are the operational answer to the harness-security critique — the container IS the trust boundary, so you can give agents full permission inside an isolated substrate without putting your laptop at risk.
